extracted.intended_audience: aspiring writers seeking literary-agent representation (fiction and narrative non-fiction)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and revising query letters to pitch manuscripts to literary agents, using agent feedback and industry resources to improve chances of representation. Covers common pitfalls, revision practices, and when to persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: What a query letter is and why you need one
rubrics_metrics.description: What a query letter is and why you need one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand the purpose of a query letter as the primary pitch to agents; the episode explains why having a query is necessary before approaching agents or submitting your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query pitfalls and pointers so you can make yours shine
rubrics_metrics.description: Query pitfalls and pointers so you can make yours shine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn common mistakes to avoid and practical pointers to improve clarity and appeal; the podcast discusses typical problems and how to fix them so queries stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query Shark critiques and step-by-step revisions (from 'meh' to 'YES')
rubrics_metrics.description: The Query Shark blog posts and critiques query letters (with permission) and shows step-by-step revisions that took a query letter from “meh” to a resounding “YES.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete critique examples and before/after revisions as a model for iterative improvement—revise your query based on agent-style feedback and compare revisions to successful outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: What happens after your query gets accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: What happens after your query gets accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be informed about post-acceptance steps (agent response, next stages in submission/representation); the episode covers expectations and likely processes after an agent says yes.

rubrics_metrics.name: When persistence pays off and when it doesn’t
rubrics_metrics.description: When persistence pays off and when it doesn’t.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a querying strategy that balances persistence with realistic stopping points; the interview addresses how to judge when to keep querying versus when to change approach or stop.

rubrics_metrics.name: Janet Reid’s #1 tip for writers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Heed top-priority advice from an experienced agent—this single tip is highlighted in the episode as particularly important for writers to adopt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use agent-run resources (Query Shark, agency blog, social media) to learn query craft
rubrics_metrics.description: To learn about Janet, follow her on Facebook and Twitter, or visit her literary agency blog or her website. You can also find her query-related pearls of wisdom on her Query Shark blog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult agent-authored blogs and social media for ongoing, practical guidance and real-world examples; these resources provide actionable insights and sample critiques to emulate.
